parsed.elsewhere_quote: Conversely, if $S$ meets every member of $\mathcal F$, choose an integer $x\ge a_1$ with support $S$. Every accepted integer smaller than $x$ has support in $\mathcal F$, and thus is noncoprime to $x$. Hence the greedy scan accepts $x$, proving $S\in\mathcal F$.
parsed.explanation: The objection is locally right: the sentence before (2) only argues that each member of F contains a minimal member. But the write-up proves the self-duality (1) in both directions immediately above, including the converse direction (a set meeting every member of F is in F). Upward-closedness is then immediate: if S contains C in 𝓒 ⊆ F, then since C meets every R in F, so does S, hence S in F by (1). Both ingredients (C ⊆ F, and the converse of (1)) are written out for all cases, so (2) and the characterization L6.1 stand as written; the omission is a one-line composition of already-proved statements.
